extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to Royal Society journals (researchers and corresponding authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting manuscripts to Royal Society journals, covering formatting, ethical statements, data and code sharing, figures/tables, peer review options, and publication/licensing requirements. Intended to ensure submissions meet editorial, ethical and technical standards for rapid assessment and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding on authorship and other contributors please consider equity, diversity and inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of authors should meet criteria on the authorship policy page; contributors who do not meet authorship criteria should be listed in acknowledgements. Follow the authorship policy linked on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitting author will be required to provide an Open Researcher and Contributor ID (ORCID) via the online submission system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision of ORCIDs by co-authors is strongly encouraged but not mandatory. The page links to benefits of registering an ORCID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-specific length and article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that length restrictions (if any), article types and other journal specific information are available on the 'Author information' page on each journal website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the specific journal's author information for exact length limits and article type definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening for plagiarism and image integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are routinely screened for plagiarism and, where relevant, image integrity (e.g. paper-mills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for routine screening; ensure originality and accurate representation of images and data to avoid editorial sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please refer to our policy on the use of Artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-assisted technologies in preparing your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will be required to declare AI use (see End section statements). Read the full policy for allowed and disallowed uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suggestions encouraged (diversity)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are encouraged to suggest suitably qualified reviewers, especially from underrepresented groups (including women, ethnic minority scientists, scientists with disabilities and other underrepresented groups), early career researchers, and researchers from the global South.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may still choose other reviewers. Suggestions should be suitably qualified; diversity is encouraged but not mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence to publish
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are required to grant us a licence to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should read the licence carefully before submission. Open access licences (e.g. CC-BY) and journal-specific options are explained on the open access and licence pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society journals only accept submissions in English. Spelling should be British English. Abbreviations should be used only when necessary and should be defined when they are first used. SI units should be used throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure British spelling and define abbreviations on first use. Use SI units uniformly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language editing recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who believe their manuscripts would benefit from professional editing prior to submission are encouraged to use a language editing service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Royal Society has negotiated discounts with some providers (AJE, Charlesworth); Royal Society Open Science partnered with PaperPal Preflight. AuthorAid and other resources are suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-free initial submission (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Format-free initial submission is introduced for the majority of journals, apart from Proceedings B and Biology Letters which require a Word version upon initial submission to enable accurate length estimation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At first submission, manuscripts can be in any format though authors are encouraged to consider readability for reviewers. Specific journals may require particular formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final submission editable files required
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an article has been accepted for publication the main manuscript must be submitted as an editable file, not a PDF, and the source files of any figures and tables must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At final revision provide editable manuscript and source files; LaTeX users should follow LaTeX guidelines. Figures/tables must be provided in editable/separate formats as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Your article title should be a short description of the research you are reporting. The title page should also contain full names and affiliations for each author, except for papers submitted to Proceedings B and Notes & Records which operate double anonymous peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best titles are written for both human readers and search engines; include keywords; avoid excessively long titles. Follow double-anonymous exceptions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be no more than 200 words and should not contain references or unexplained abbreviations or acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should be concise, informative, standalone, summarise scope, main results and conclusions, and include likely search terms. Consider IMRAD framework. The abstract provided at initial submission is included in reviewer invitation emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include at least 3 and up to 10 keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly broad or specialised terms; think of search terms you would use; keywords can be short phrases and include synonyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main text structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The main text of your article should be split into clearly-labelled sections (usually background, methods, results, discussion and conclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use headings/subheadings that best suit the article; abbreviations should be written out in full on first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods section completeness and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods section should contain all elements necessary to allow interpretation and replication of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full details of materials (reagents, animal models, software), references to published methods or protocols (e.g. protocols.io), encourage preregistration, include accession details where appropriate, and provide a Data Availability statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field Stations and Marine Laboratories acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where authors have conducted research at or with the support of FSMLs etc, we encourage authors to provide the names and locations of FSMLs etc in both the methods and acknowledgements sections of their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal recognition helps tracking outputs and justifying budgets. The page includes a sample sentence example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Please acknowledge anyone who contributed to the study but did not meet the authorship criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List non-author contributors in the acknowledgements section rather than as authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Please state the sources of funding including grant number for each author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many funders require this. The page suggests a standard format: e.g. 'This work was supported by the Wellcome Trust [grant numbers xxxx, yyyy]; ...' and authors will also enter funding info during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: References style and dataset citation
rubrics_metrics.description: All our journals use a system based on Vancouver style referencing; references will be given in the order of their appearance in the text in a consecutively numbered list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to datasets must also be included in the reference list with DOIs where available. Each reference should include as many elements as possible: author surnames/initials, year, title, journal name abbreviation, volume number, publisher/location, page numbers or article number, DOI. EndNote style files available for many journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX guidelines and required files
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit a PDF as your main document. At final revision you will also be required to provide the source files. TeX files submitted should preferably be generated using pdfTeX (TeX Live 2024/2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All files required to compile TeX source must be uploaded: input Tex file and input PDF, .bib or .bbl file, .bst file if style specified. Do not send master TeX files containing file call-ups (except to figures and references); the TeX file must be complete with all article sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must be supplied as gif, tiff, jpg, png, ps or eps files, and should be a single flattened layer. Type 3 fonts are not accepted. Vector fonts (Type1, truetype, opentype etc.) are preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX/LaTeX-coded figures should be converted to postscript format (PS or EPS). Guidelines for document and image conversions are provided in ScholarOne Manuscripts help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code sharing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a requirement of Royal Society Publishing that data and code underlying a study are made publicly available, usually within a designated repository or from the supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must complete the data accessibility section in the submission form; it is not permitted to state that data will be available from the authors upon request. See the full data sharing policy for repositories and guidance around restricted data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material can be used for supporting data sets, supporting movies, figures and tables, and any other supporting material; the main article should stand on its own merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger datasets should be uploaded to a repository rather than provided as supplementary material. Supplementary material is created by authors and is not edited by the Royal Society; proof-read carefully. Supplementary files published under CC-BY, files up to 350MB (contact editorial office for larger files). Supplementary files posted on figshare and will receive a DOI; provide accurate titles and descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and tables numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures and tables should be numbered and cited in the text. Figure and table captions are required and should be brief and informative and include any relevant copyright information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At initial submission, figures can be within the manuscript or separate. Images should be minimally processed and accurately reflect the original data; authors should retain unprocessed data and metadata as editors may request them. Final submission: figures as separate files and tables in editable format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure formats (final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure formats: PNG, EPS, TIFF, JPG, JPEG. TeX/LaTeX-coded figures should be converted to postscript format (PS or EPS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide figures in the required formats at final submission. Ensure fonts and layers are compatible (single flattened layer preferred).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested style for figure labels and numeric formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested style for figure labels: Font Times New Roman; 9pt, 11pt leading preferred; text can be reduced but should be no smaller than 7.5pt. Numbers and units: use a thin space between values and units (e.g. 300 nm). Thousands separated by thin spaces, not commas (e.g. 10 000 000). Equal-to sign: insert a full space either side (e.g. x = 300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multipart figures: parts labelled alphabetically and consistently (left to right, top to bottom); labels in same position; if interfering with content, place outside figure part (top left); alphabetical labels italicized in roman brackets '(a)'; sub-parts with bracketed roman numerals '(ii)'. Labels on coloured backgrounds should be placed inside a white circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure permissions and third‑party material
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures from other sources should be fully acknowledged in the caption, and written permission sought for both print and electronic reproduction before being used (where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publishing open access under CC-BY, third party material will also fall under this licence and permission must be obtained. If material cannot be included under CC-BY, identify this in the text (e.g., add copyright info to caption) or inform production team.

rubrics_metrics.name: End section statements required at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the submission process in ScholarOne, you will be required to provide statements on ethics, use of AI, data/code/materials, competing interests and CRediT contributor roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statements are essential for rapid assessment and will be automatically added to the paper if accepted; authors are no longer required to add these statements in the manuscript itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics statement detail requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on humans or human tissues will require a statement detailing ethical approval (including the name of the research body that granted approval and the project/licence number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also detail whether informed consent was obtained and by whom. For animal studies, include ethical approval details and licence/approval numbers. List fieldwork approvals and specimen details (museum specimen numbers and holding institutions) either in manuscript or supplementary files.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use declaration (end section)
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be asked to declare whether you have used AI technologies in the preparation of your paper. If you have, please provide a statement about how you have used this – the statement will be published in the final article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the full AI policy for details of allowed use; transparent declaration is mandatory where AI was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, code and materials statement guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers that report primary data will require a section that states where the article's supporting data, materials and code can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deposited in an external repository list the database, accession number and relevant details; datasets included in repositories must also be listed in the reference section. Examples of acceptable dataset citations are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Please provide a statement if you have any competing interests to declare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests are defined as those that could undermine the objectivity, integrity or perceived value of publication. Contact the editorial office for advice if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitting author will be required to allocate roles to authors from a taxonomy of 14 roles to create an Authors' Contributions section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles include: Conceptualization; Data curation; Formal analysis; Funding acquisition; Investigation; Methodology; Project administration; Resources; Software; Supervision; Validation; Visualization; Writing – original draft; Writing – review & editing. More information is linked (https://credit.niso.org/).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to Royal Society science journals are normally peer reviewed in a single-anonymized fashion (author names are not concealed, but referee names are).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee reports and correspondence must remain confidential and should not be shared unless the journal is operating under open/Transparent peer review. Open peer review is optional for Proceedings A and mandatory for Proceedings B, Open Biology, Royal Society Open Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence to publish and open access details
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society Open Science and Open Biology are fully open access journals; other journals are open access through Subscribe to Open in 2026. Open access papers are published under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC-BY) licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC-BY allows copying, distribution, transmission and adaptation with attribution. Authors must grant the licence; note implications for third-party material and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article transfer policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers may be offered when an article does not meet the scope requirement of the original journal. Editors' comments and reviewer reports on the article are transferred over and will be available to the editorial team of the receiving journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer is usually quicker than resubmission; transferring is a two-step process and should be completed promptly (offer expires after four weeks). A list of possible transfers between specific journals is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting final files for publication you will be prompted to submit a media summary of no more than 100 words aimed at a lay audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline research and relevant findings, highlight why research is important, link to examples or analogies, avoid excessive jargon or statistics. Ensure contact details are up to date for press enquiries; the Society's press office will manage embargoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover image submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You are welcome to submit a potential cover image for use on the journal website and press site for media promotion of your article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you obtain all relevant copyright permissions before submitting; upload potential images when submitting revised files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofing procedure and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author will be sent a link to review the article proof; proofs should be read carefully and the accuracy of tables, references and mathematical expressions checked. Major alterations to content should not be made at this stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofing uses Kriyadocs platform; changes/queries are tracked. Only a few days may be available for checking proofs; arrange for alternative proof checking if absent. Send production queries to proofs@royalsociety.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprint and reuse restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: On publication, authors will be provided with a link providing free access to the paper; these electronic reprints may NOT be used for commercial purposes or posted on openly accessible websites unless published under a CC-BY licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of printed issues may be purchased on request; contact sales team for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and media embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to share and promote their work, but the Society employs a strict embargo policy whereby reporting of a scientific article by the media is embargoed until a specific time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approached by a journalist prior to publication contact the press office. Alert your institution's press office in advance if possible to coordinate press releases with the Society's embargo schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online article seminars encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to give an online seminar about their accepted article; author seminars are given a DOI and listed on the Cassyni seminar collection page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Society for more information about seminars and listing.
